domains.mcu: Always-on MCU-side logic; +3.3V_MCU. High-side control/fault paths also reach a separately powered protection IC.
domains.external-control: Host UART into the MCU domain; the external host may drive independently.
domains.ground: Hard-grounded buffer input; this is not a dedicated connector ground contact.
domains.switched-logic: Peripheral-side +3.3V_SW logic, including filtered rails; supplies are checked separately.
domains.switched-5v-pgood: Open-drain power-good with pull-up to +5V_SW; input nominal high is 5 V, buffer output is 3.3 V.
domains.switched-12v-pgood: Power-good with 10k/4.7k divider from +12V to ground; input high is a divided rail, not MCU logic.

mcu-on-switched-off.assumptions: All attached outputs are high impedance; rails have settled. This is a passive bias inventory, not a reset or power-off qualification.

all-rails-on.assumptions: All attached outputs are high impedance; rails have settled. This is a passive bias inventory, not a reset or power-off qualification.

all-rails-off.assumptions: All attached outputs are high impedance and every declared rail is at ground. Buffers are unpowered: the calculated input bias does not imply a valid connector reading.

DIG0.notes: Boot beacon clock or firmware marker depending on phase/build; no series input tap.

DIG1.notes: Boot beacon data or runtime QS TX depending on phase/build; no independent runtime trigger while tracing.

DIG2.notes: Tap is on the MCU side of the pyControl boundary series resistor.

DIG3.notes: External host can override the passive pull-up. This is board RX despite the DIO-A connector name.

DIG15.notes: Conditioned limit switch goes to the TMC, not an MCU GPIO.

DIG21.notes: A low passive bias is not proof of a brake fault while the switched domain is off.

DIG22.notes: Recipe/profile alias DAQ_SDA maps to functional DAC_SDA through the board source.

DIG23.notes: Recipe/profile alias DAQ_SCL maps to functional DAC_SCL through the board source.

DIG24.notes: MCU-side command tap; does not directly measure the switched HV rail.

DIG25.notes: No external DC pull reaches this tap; internal DIAG_EN behavior is not inferred by the resistor model.

DIG26.notes: Biased toward +3.3V_MCU through protection-series and pull-up resistors; not a guaranteed fault verdict during supply transitions.

DIG27.notes: R607 7.87k pulls the switch enable high; outputs from firmware or a debugger can override it.

DIG28.notes: Conditioned encoder A goes to the TMC, not an MCU GPIO.

DIG29.notes: Conditioned encoder B goes to the TMC, not an MCU GPIO.

DIG30.notes: Direct buffer input, no input tap resistor. Pull-up source is +5V_SW.

DIG31.notes: Direct buffer input, no input tap resistor. R1902/R1903 form the 12 V divider; DIG31 is connected, not grounded.

SN74LV541ARKSR.scope: Pin pairs, enables, power supply and partial power down. Board leakage/transition behavior remains unqualified.

SN74CB3Q3245RGYR.scope: A/B pairing and active-low enable. Model traverses only explicitly declared switches.

limits: Connectivity is checked against exported XML and saved PCB pad assignments, not copper geometry.
Resistor values and population are current schematic declarations, not a manufacturing/assembly comparison.
Bias scenarios assume all attached drivers are high impedance and the declared rails have settled.
Resistor paths describe topology; mixed rails require a divider/leakage/threshold analysis.
Observed logic, reset transitions, leakage, probe loading and power-off behavior are not qualified.
An unpowered observation buffer does not provide a valid logic reading, even for grounded inputs.
Direction/domain labels are board declarations; supply checks and pin endpoints are connectivity evidence.
